question: During the In-Vehicle/Engine Start inspection, which of the following is NOT one of the dashboard lighting indicators the driver must inspect?
choice_a: ABS indicator on dashboard
choice_c: Odometer reading
choice_d: Left turn signal indicator
explanation: The manual lists left/right turn signal indicators, the four-way emergency indicator, high beam headlight indicator, ABS indicator, and DEF indicator as required lighting indicators; the odometer is not part of this inspection.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Lighting Indicators

question: Which items make up the required emergency equipment inspected during the internal (in-vehicle) inspection?
choice_a: First aid kit, tow chain, and flashlight
choice_b: Spare electrical fuses or circuit breakers, a properly charged and secured fire extinguisher, and three red reflective triangles (or fusees/liquid burning flares)
choice_c: Spare tire, jack, and tool kit
choice_d: Jumper cables and a tire gauge
explanation: The manual requires inspecting for spare fuses or circuit breakers, a charged and secured fire extinguisher, and warning devices (three red reflective triangles, six fusee flares, or three liquid burning flares).
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Emergency Equipment

question: How many red reflective triangles must a CDL vehicle carry if that is the type of warning device it uses?
choice_a: Four
choice_c: Six
choice_d: Three
explanation: The manual specifies three red reflective triangles (as an alternative to six fusee flares or three liquid burning flares).
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Emergency Equipment

question: If a vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, what must the driver identify to the examiner?
choice_a: That the fire extinguisher is a substitute
choice_b: That the vehicle operates on circuit breakers instead
choice_c: That the vehicle cannot be inspected
choice_d: That the vehicle needs replacement fuses before testing
explanation: The manual states that if the vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, the driver must mention this and identify that the vehicle operates on circuit breakers.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Emergency Equipment

question: What must be true of the windshield during the internal inspection?
choice_a: It must have a manufacturer sticker visible
choice_b: It only needs to be free of large cracks
choice_c: It must have tinted glass on all sides
choice_d: It must be clean with no obstructions except an inspection sticker, with no damage such as cracks or flaws
explanation: The manual requires the windshield to be clean with no obstructions (except an inspection sticker) and free of damage such as cracks or flaws.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Windshield and Traffic Monitoring Devices

question: Why is the horn inspected on a commercial motor vehicle?
choice_a: It must function properly to warn other roadway users and avoid potential collisions
choice_b: It alerts passengers of arrival at a stop
choice_c: It is required only for weigh station identification
choice_d: It indicates when the parking brake is engaged
explanation: The manual explains the horn must function properly to warn cars, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians of the driver's presence and avoid potential collisions.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Horn(s)

question: During the Parking Brake check, what must the driver do after engaging the parking brake?
choice_a: Drive at highway speed and apply the parking brake suddenly
choice_b: Check only the parking brake fluid reservoir
choice_c: Release the parking brake and coast downhill
choice_d: Remove foot from the service brake and gently pull forward to inspect that the parking brake holds the vehicle
explanation: The manual requires removing the foot from the service brake and gently pulling forward with the parking brake engaged to confirm it holds the vehicle.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: During the Trailer Brake check on a combination vehicle, what is the correct brake configuration?
choice_a: Both the parking brake and trailer parking brake engaged
choice_b: Parking brake engaged and trailer parking brake released
choice_c: Both the parking brake and trailer parking brake released
choice_d: Parking brake released and trailer parking brake engaged
explanation: The manual specifies releasing the tractor parking brake while the trailer parking brake is engaged, then pulling forward gently to confirm the trailer brake holds.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: Besides confirming the trailer parking brake holds the vehicle, what else does the Trailer Brake check help verify?
choice_a: Tire tread depth
choice_c: The coupling connection with the trailer
choice_d: DEF fluid quality
explanation: The manual notes that the trailer brake check also assists in checking the coupling connection with the trailer.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: During the Service Brake Check, at approximately what speed should the driver pull forward before applying the service brake?
choice_a: 25 mph
choice_c: 5 mph
choice_d: 35 mph
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service (foot) brake, and come to a complete stop.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.1 - Service Brake Check

question: How many parts of the air brake check must be correctly explained and demonstrated to avoid an automatic failure?
choice_a: Two
choice_c: Five
choice_d: Four
explanation: The manual states that failure to explain and demonstrate all four parts of the air brake check correctly results in automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check

question: During the Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check, at approximately what psi range does governor cutout typically occur?
explanation: The manual states the governor cutout occurs at approximately 120-140 psi, or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check, Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check

question: During the Air Leakage Rate Test on a single vehicle (or a trailer without air brakes), what is the maximum allowed air pressure drop in one minute after stabilization?
choice_a: 2 pounds
choice_c: 4 pounds
choice_d: 1 pound
explanation: The manual specifies the air pressure must not drop more than three pounds in one minute for a single vehicle or trailer without air brakes.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check, Air Leakage Rate Test

question: During the Air Leakage Rate Test on a combination vehicle, what is the maximum allowed air pressure drop in one minute after stabilization?
choice_a: 4 pounds
choice_c: 3 pounds
choice_d: 5 pounds
explanation: For a combination vehicle, the manual allows no more than four pounds of pressure drop in one minute after initial stabilization.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check, Air Leakage Rate Test

question: During the Air Warning Device(s) Test, at what psi level should the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, flag) activate?
choice_a: Before pressure drops below 55 psi
choice_c: Before pressure drops below 75 psi
choice_d: Before pressure drops below 20 psi
explanation: The manual states the low air warning devices should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check, Air Warning Device(s) Test

question: During the Emergency Brake(s) Test, between what psi range should the parking (or emergency) brake valve close ('pop out')?
explanation: The manual specifies the valve should close (pop out) between 20 psi and 45 psi, or at the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check, Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: On air-operated trailers, when should the tractor protection valve and trailer parking brake valve pop out relative to the truck/tractor valve?
choice_a: Only after the trailer physically detaches
choice_b: At the same time or prior to the valve for the truck/tractor/bus
choice_c: They never pop out on trailers
choice_d: Well after the truck/tractor valve pops out
explanation: The manual states the tractor protection valve and trailer parking brake valve should close at the same time or prior to the valve for the truck/tractor/bus.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check, Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: If a vehicle is equipped with a primary and secondary air brake system, what must the driver explain about a loss of pressure in only one system?
choice_a: The vehicle must be towed immediately
choice_b: There is a backup system, so the valve(s) will not pop out due to loss of pressure in only one system
choice_c: Both systems will fail immediately together
choice_d: The parking brake will fully engage regardless
explanation: The manual requires the driver to explain that a backup system exists and the valves will not pop out from a pressure loss in only one of the two systems.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check, Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: What happens if a driver fails to properly explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check?
choice_a: An automatic retest is scheduled
choice_c: No penalty, since it is optional
choice_d: Automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
explanation: The manual states that failure to explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check correctly results in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: With the transmission in 'park,' how many times should the driver pump the brake pedal before holding it down, per the hydraulic brake check procedure?
choice_a: Five times
choice_c: Three times
choice_d: One time
explanation: The manual instructs pumping the brake pedal three times, then holding it down for five seconds (or as specified by the manufacturer).
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: After pumping the brake pedal three times during the hydraulic brake check, how long should the driver hold it down?
choice_a: 10 seconds
choice_c: 15 seconds
choice_d: 5 seconds
explanation: The manual specifies holding the brake pedal down for five seconds after pumping it three times.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: What should NOT happen to the brake pedal after its initial application during the hydraulic brake check?
choice_a: It should have reserve pressure
choice_c: It should remain at a steady height
choice_d: It should feel firm
explanation: The manual states the brake pedal should not move (depress) after initial application and should be firm with sufficient reserve.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: What must be inspected about bus entry doors during the Passenger Entry and Lift inspection?
choice_a: That they are painted a matching color
choice_b: That they are not damaged, operate smoothly, and close securely from the inside
choice_c: That they lock automatically once the bus exceeds 20 mph
choice_d: That they have tinted glass
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that entry doors are not damaged, operate smoothly, and close securely from the inside.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.2 - Passenger Entry and Lift

question: If a bus is equipped with a passenger lift, what must be confirmed about the lift when it is not in use?
choice_a: It must be fully retracted and latched securely
choice_b: It must be disconnected from the electrical system
choice_c: It must be folded and covered with a tarp
choice_d: It must be removed from the vehicle entirely
explanation: The manual states that, if equipped, the lift must be fully retracted and latched securely.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.2 - Passenger Entry and Lift

question: How many emergency exits must the driver actually demonstrate operate smoothly, close securely, and are not damaged?
choice_a: At least one
choice_c: Exactly two
choice_d: All of them
explanation: The manual requires demonstrating that at least one emergency exit operates smoothly, closes securely, and is not damaged, while pointing out and describing how the others operate.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.2 - Emergency Exits

question: Why must passenger seat frames be inspected on a passenger or school bus?
choice_a: To check for hidden storage compartments
choice_c: Seats must be safe for passengers, so frames must not be broken and must be firmly attached to the floor
choice_d: To verify seat color coding
explanation: The manual explains that seats must be safe for passengers to sit in, requiring inspection for broken frames and secure attachment to the floor.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.2 - Passenger Seating

question: Which specific mirrors must be inspected on a school bus in addition to standard passenger and external mirrors?
choice_a: Undercarriage mirrors
choice_c: Student crossover mirrors
choice_d: Rear bumper cameras
explanation: The manual specifically calls out inspecting student crossover mirrors on school buses only.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.2 - Passenger Monitoring Devices

question: Why must internal and external passenger mirrors or monitoring devices be inspected on a passenger or school bus?
choice_a: To assist with parallel parking only
choice_c: To help the driver safely observe boarding and discharging passengers or students
choice_d: To detect low tire pressure
explanation: The manual explains these devices help the driver safely observe and monitor passengers or students during driving, loading, and unloading.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.2 - Passenger Monitoring Devices

question: What is the purpose of the alternately flashing amber and red student lights on a school bus?
choice_a: To communicate the bus's presence and intentions to stop or resume student loading/unloading with other traffic
choice_b: To illuminate the roadway at night
choice_c: To indicate the bus is out of service
choice_d: To indicate the bus is low on fuel
explanation: The manual states student lights allow the driver to communicate presence and intentions regarding student loading/unloading to other traffic.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.3 - Student Lights (Front and Back)

question: Which student lights must be inspected and demonstrated on BOTH the front and back of a school bus?
choice_a: Strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights
choice_c: Only headlights
choice_d: Only turn signals
explanation: The manual requires inspecting the strobe light (if equipped), flashing amber lights, and flashing red lights on both the front and back of the bus, along with their dash indicators.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.3 - Student Lights (Front and Back)

question: What is the function of the school bus Stop Arm?
choice_a: It displays the bus route number
choice_b: It warns other drivers that a school bus is stopping or is stopped
choice_c: It indicates the bus is low on fuel
choice_d: It signals a mechanical failure to other drivers
explanation: The manual states the Stop Arm warns other drivers that a school bus is stopping or is stopped.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.3 - Stop Arm(s) and Safety Arm

question: What is the function of the Safety Arm on a school bus, as distinct from the Stop Arm?
choice_a: It forces students to cross a safe distance (e.g., 10 feet) away from the front of the bus, within the driver's view
choice_b: It provides additional braking force to the rear wheels
choice_c: It holds the stop sign in place when retracted
choice_d: It supports the front bumper structurally
explanation: The manual explains the Safety Arm forces school students to cross well (e.g., 10 feet) away from the front of the school bus in the driver's view.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.3 - Stop Arm(s) and Safety Arm

question: How can a driver tell that a school bus's first aid kit or body fluid cleanup kit may be missing items?
choice_a: By checking an expiration date printed on the kit
choice_c: By counting the number of bandages inside
choice_d: If the seal on the kit has been broken
explanation: The manual states to inspect that the kit is present and the seal has not been broken, which may indicate missing items.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.3 - First Aid Emergency and Body Fluid Kits

question: Which lights must be inspected as operating and illuminating during the Lights Operations Check?
choice_a: Left/right turn signals, 4-way flashers, low and high beam headlights, clearance/marker lights, taillights, and brake lights
choice_c: Only clearance lights
choice_d: Only brake lights
explanation: The manual lists all of these lights on the front, sides, and rear of the vehicle as required to be inspected for proper operation.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.4 - Lights Operations Check

question: On a combination vehicle, which part of the trailer must be inspected during the Lights Operations Check?
choice_a: The entire trailer roof
choice_c: The rear of the trailer
choice_d: The front of the trailer only
explanation: The manual notes that on a combination vehicle, the driver need only inspect the rear of the trailer for the lights check.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.4 - Lights Operations Check

question: From where must the operation of all external lights be inspected?
choice_a: Via a diagnostic scan tool
choice_b: Via the dashboard indicator lights only
choice_c: From inside the vehicle cab only
choice_d: From outside the vehicle
explanation: The manual states the operation of all external lights must be inspected from outside the vehicle, including lights activated by an automated light check system.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.4 - Lights Operations Check

question: What is the driver's responsibility while the examiner observes the lights from outside the vehicle?
choice_a: Exit the vehicle and personally point at each light
choice_b: Nothing further is required once the examiner steps outside
choice_c: Roll down the window and clearly direct the examiner to exactly which lights to inspect as they are activated
choice_d: Honk the horn once for each light being tested
explanation: The manual states the driver must roll the window down and speak loudly enough to direct the examiner to the specific lights being activated.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.4 - Lights Operations Check

question: What must happen to the brake lights during the Lights Operations Check?
choice_a: They must flash regardless of brake status
choice_b: They must stay on continuously regardless of brake application
choice_c: They must only illuminate at night
choice_d: They must come on when brakes are applied and turn off when brakes are released
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that brake lights come on when the brakes are applied and turn off when the brakes are released.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.4 - Lights Operations Check

question: What must be true of light lenses or covers on the front of the vehicle/tractor?
choice_a: They must be replaced every calendar year
choice_b: They must carry a manufacturer decal
choice_c: They must be tinted for glare reduction
choice_d: They must be the proper color, clean, not broken, and not missing
explanation: The manual requires that light lenses or covers be the proper color, clean, and free of damage or missing parts.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Lenses (Front of Vehicle)

question: Which fluid levels must be identified as inspected, with the engine off, during the Front of Vehicle/Engine Area inspection?
choice_a: Only engine oil
choice_b: Windshield washer fluid and antifreeze only
choice_c: Transmission fluid and differential fluid
choice_d: Engine oil, cooling system/coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid (hydraulic brakes only)
explanation: The manual lists engine oil, coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid (for hydraulic brake systems) as the critical fluid levels to identify.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Critical Fluid Levels

question: What caution does the manual give regarding checking the coolant level?
choice_a: Do not remove the radiator cap if the engine is hot
choice_b: Only check coolant in cold weather
choice_c: Always check coolant with the engine running
choice_d: Always add coolant before checking the level
explanation: The manual specifically cautions that if the engine is hot, the driver should not remove the radiator cap.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Critical Fluid Levels

question: Where should a driver look when inspecting for fluid leaks under the vehicle?
choice_a: For puddles on the ground and dripping fluids around/on the underside of the engine and transmission
choice_b: Only at the fuel filler cap
choice_c: Only at the exhaust pipe
choice_d: Only inside the cab near the pedals
explanation: The manual instructs looking for puddles on the ground and dripping fluids around and on the underside of the engine and transmission.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Fluid and Air Leaks

question: Why are worn, cracked, loose, or broken steering parts a serious safety concern?
choice_a: They could result in loss of steering, and movement in the linkage can cause wandering or other control problems
choice_c: They only cause uneven tire wear with no control impact
choice_d: They have no measurable safety impact
explanation: The manual explains that worn or damaged steering parts could result in loss of steering and cause the vehicle to wander or experience other control problems.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Steering System

question: What must be inspected regarding the power steering box?
choice_a: That it has a matching paint finish
choice_b: That it is securely mounted and not leaking
choice_c: That it is the same brand as the engine
choice_d: That it carries a valid warranty sticker
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the power steering box is securely mounted and not leaking.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Steering System

question: What must be verified regarding nuts, bolts, or cotter keys/pins in the steering connections?
choice_a: That they are all the same brand
choice_c: That they are replaced every year regardless of condition
choice_d: That they are color-coded by torque value
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that there are no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys/pins in the steering connections.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Steering System

question: What tool must a driver mention using to check tire inflation in order to receive credit?
choice_a: Visual inspection alone
choice_c: A pressure washer
choice_d: A tire gauge
explanation: The manual explicitly states a driver will not get credit for simply kicking the tires or using a mallet; the use of a tire gauge must be mentioned.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Tires

question: What is the minimum tread depth requirement for steering axle tires, per the manual's inspection guidance?
choice_a: 2/32 inch
choice_c: 8/32 inch
choice_d: 6/32 inch
explanation: The manual specifies a minimum tread depth of 4/32 inch on major tread grooves containing wear bars for steering axle tires.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Tires, Tread Depth

question: What is the minimum tread depth requirement for tires on axles other than the steering axle?
choice_a: 6/32 inch
choice_c: 2/32 inch
choice_d: 1/32 inch
explanation: The manual specifies a minimum tread depth of 2/32 inch on all other (non-steering axle) tires.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Tires, Tread Depth

question: Underinflation of a tire increases the chance of what specific failure?
choice_a: A blowout from excessive heat buildup due to increased flexing
choice_c: Excessive fuel economy
choice_d: Reduced stopping ability from too much tread contact
explanation: The manual explains underinflation increases the chance of a blowout from excessive heat buildup due to increased flexing of the tire.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Tires

question: If tires are equipped with an automatic tire inflation system (ATIS) or tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) connected to the valve stems, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Still manually gauge each tire individually as usual
choice_b: Mention that tire pressure is monitored and adjusted by an automatic system, and inspect that it is working properly
choice_c: Ignore tire pressure inspection entirely
choice_d: Disconnect the system before beginning the test
explanation: The manual states that with such systems in place, the driver need only mention the automatic monitoring/adjustment and confirm it is working properly.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Tires

question: Are welding repairs permitted on a damaged or cracked rim per the inspection criteria?
choice_a: Only on dual rear rims
choice_c: No, rims cannot have welding repairs
choice_d: Yes, if performed by a certified welder
explanation: The manual explicitly states that rims cannot have welding repairs.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Rims

question: What signs during inspection may indicate a lug nut is loose?
choice_a: Rust trails or shiny threads
choice_c: A protective dust cap
choice_d: A fresh coat of paint
explanation: The manual states to inspect that lug nuts are not loose and there are no signs of rust trails or shiny threads that may show looseness.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Lug Nuts

question: What could damaged or missing leaf springs/coil springs lead to?
choice_a: Improved ride quality with no safety impact
choice_c: Loss of control or rollover if the vehicle falls on the frame or a tire
choice_d: Increased fuel economy
explanation: The manual warns that damaged or missing springs may lead to loss of control or rollover if the vehicle falls on the frame or on a tire.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Springs/Mounts, U-Bolts and Air Bags and Shocks

question: Why are brake contaminates, such as grease or oil, a safety concern?
choice_a: They only affect the vehicle's appearance
choice_c: They improve braking performance in wet conditions
choice_d: They can reduce braking friction (potentially leading to a crash) and can create a fire hazard
explanation: The manual explains that contaminates can reduce braking friction, potentially causing a crash, and can also create a fire hazard.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Brake Contaminates

question: Why are reflectors on the sides of a vehicle or trailer inspected?
choice_a: They allow the driver of a commercial vehicle to be seen and communicate presence with other traffic
choice_b: They improve aerodynamics and fuel economy
choice_c: They indicate the cargo weight class
choice_d: They are purely decorative
explanation: The manual states side reflectors allow the driver to be seen and to communicate presence with other traffic.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.3 - Lenses and Reflectors

question: What must side mirrors or other monitoring devices provide to the driver?
choice_a: Turn-by-turn navigation guidance
choice_b: A view limited to the cargo area only
choice_c: Visibility to the sides and rear of the vehicle, especially in blind areas
choice_d: A live view of the engine compartment
explanation: The manual states these devices provide visibility to the sides and rear of the vehicle, especially in blind areas, so the driver can see other traffic.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.3 - Traffic Monitoring Devices

question: Why is damage to the batteries or electrical system a safety concern?
choice_a: It only affects the radio and interior lighting
choice_c: It can cause vehicle breakdowns or an electrical shortage leading to an onboard fire
choice_d: It has no safety relevance
explanation: The manual explains that battery or electrical system damage can cause breakdowns or an electrical shortage leading to a fire onboard the vehicle.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.3 - Battery

question: Why are fuel tank/DEF tank leaks considered a hazard?
choice_a: They have no direct safety concern
choice_b: They are a fire hazard, and fuel on pavement can be very slippery, creating driving hazards
choice_c: They only reduce the vehicle's fuel range
choice_d: They only affect emissions test results
explanation: The manual states leaks are a fire hazard and can cause driving hazards to other traffic because fuel on pavement can be very slippery.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.3 - Fuel Tank/DEF Tank

question: Why could loose or cracked frame members be dangerous?
choice_a: They only cause a rattling noise while driving
choice_b: They may reduce vehicle stability and cause handling/cornering problems, including possible rollover
choice_c: They interfere with radio reception
choice_d: They have no impact on vehicle safety
explanation: The manual explains loose or cracked frame members may reduce vehicle stability, cause handling and cornering problems (e.g., wandering, possible rollover), and result in total loss of vehicle control.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.3 - Frame(s)

question: On a combination vehicle, which part must be inspected for rear lenses and reflectors?
choice_a: Only the power unit
choice_b: Only the rear of the trailer
choice_c: Both the power unit and the trailer
choice_d: This step is skipped entirely for combination vehicles
explanation: The manual notes that on a combination vehicle, the driver need only inspect the rear of the trailer for lenses and reflectors.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.4 - Rear of Vehicle or Trailer

question: What must be true of rear light lenses/covers and reflectors on the vehicle or trailer?
choice_a: They must be the proper color, clean, not broken, and not missing
choice_b: They must match the cab's paint color
choice_c: They must be tinted to reduce glare
choice_d: They must be replaced annually regardless of condition
explanation: The manual requires that rear lenses/covers and reflectors be the proper color, clean, and free of damage or missing parts.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.5.4 - Rear of Vehicle or Trailer

question: What could result from a low air condition causing sudden loss of air to the trailer's brakes?
choice_a: No effect, since trailer brakes are fully independent
choice_b: An automatic downshift of the transmission
choice_c: Improved trailer braking performance
choice_d: Sudden application of the trailer's spring brakes, possibly resulting in loss of control and a crash
explanation: The manual warns that a low air condition will cause sudden application of the trailer's spring brakes, which may result in loss of control and lead to a crash.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: What could result from a damaged electric line connection to the trailer?
choice_a: Only the interior radio losing power
choice_b: Total loss of braking and control to the towed unit, potentially leading to a crash
choice_c: No significant effect on trailer operation
choice_d: Automatic disconnection of the trailer
explanation: The manual states loss of electrical connection to the trailer results in total loss of braking and control to the towed unit and can lead to a crash.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: What must be verified about air and electric connectors on the power unit and trailer?
choice_a: That they are seated and sealed, free of damage, and locked into place
choice_b: That they can be removed without any tools
choice_c: That they are painted matching colors
choice_d: That they are wrapped in electrical tape for protection
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that connectors on both the power unit and trailer are seated and sealed, free of damage, and locked into place.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: What condition must NOT be present on air hoses and electrical lines connecting a power unit and trailer?
choice_a: Any bends around the frame rail
choice_c: Cuts, cracks, chafing, splices, tape, or wear where the steel braid/electrical conductor shows through
choice_d: Standard color coding
explanation: The manual states hoses and lines must not be cut, cracked, chafed, spliced, taped, or worn such that the steel braid or electrical conductor shows through.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: To receive credit for inspecting the air and electric line connections on a combination vehicle, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Inspect only the power unit side connections
choice_b: Inspect only the trailer side connections
choice_c: Inspect the connections on both the power unit and the trailer
choice_d: Describe the connections verbally without touching or pointing to them
explanation: The manual notes the driver must inspect the connections on both the power unit and trailer to receive credit.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: What could a faulty or damaged fifth wheel skid plate result in?
choice_a: No meaningful safety impact
choice_c: Better fuel economy for the tractor
choice_d: Handling problems, rollover, or separation of the tractor and trailer leading to a crash
explanation: The manual warns that a faulty or damaged fifth wheel skid plate can result in handling problems, rollover, or separation of the tractor and trailer, leading to a crash.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Fifth Wheel Skid Plate

question: When inspecting the kingpin, apron, and gap on a fifth wheel combination, what must be verified?
choice_a: That the apron is disconnected from the trailer
choice_b: That the kingpin is removed during inspection for cleaning
choice_c: That there is a visible one-inch gap left for lubrication
choice_d: That the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no space (gap) between the apron and fifth wheel
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the trailer lies flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap between the apron and fifth wheel.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Kingpin, Apron & Gap

question: What must be inspected on a pintle hook coupling?
choice_a: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle frame, with no loose or missing mounting bolts, nuts, pins, brackets, or clamps
choice_b: That it swivels freely a full 360 degrees
choice_c: That it is painted a specific safety color
choice_d: That it carries a visible manufacturer decal
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the pintle hook is securely mounted to the vehicle frame with no loose or missing parts, and checking for cracks, breaks, or excessive wear.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Pintle Hook

question: For a tow/receiver hitch combination, what additional item does the manual specifically call out to inspect if equipped?
choice_a: The sway bar/control
choice_c: The mud flap brackets
choice_d: The truck bed liner
explanation: The manual specifically notes to inspect the sway bar/control, if equipped, when inspecting the tow hitch.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Tow Hitch

question: For fifth wheel coupling systems, what must the driver look for when inspecting the locking jaws or lever through the fifth wheel gap?
choice_a: That the locking jaws have been removed for cleaning
choice_b: That the locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin with no play between the kingpin and locking jaws/lever
choice_c: That the gap is completely filled with grease
choice_d: That there is visible daylight around the kingpin
explanation: The manual requires looking into the fifth wheel gap to inspect that the locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin with no play.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Locking and Safety Devices

question: What must be true of safety cables or chains on a combination vehicle coupling, if present?
choice_a: They are optional equipment and not part of the inspection
choice_b: They must be a specific bright color for visibility
choice_c: They must be secure, crossed, and free of kinks and excessive slack, with any breakaway cables engaged
choice_d: They must be left loose to allow for sharp turns
explanation: The manual requires that safety cables or chains be secure, crossed, and free of kinks and excessive slack, and that breakaway cables must be engaged.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Locking and Safety Devices

question: Why must trailer landing gear be fully raised before travel?
choice_a: To make future hitching easier
choice_b: To improve the tractor's fuel economy
choice_c: To reduce the overall trailer weight
choice_d: So it will not strike the ground during travel and will clear the back of the power unit while turning
explanation: The manual states landing gear must be raised properly so it will not strike the ground during travel and must clear the back of the power unit while turning.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.2 - Landing Gear & Clearance

question: What is the purpose of reflective tape on the sides and rear of a trailer?
choice_a: It improves the trailer's aerodynamics
choice_b: It is purely a decorative or branding element
choice_c: It indicates the trailer's weight classification
choice_d: It allows the driver of a commercial vehicle to be seen and to communicate presence with other traffic
explanation: The manual explains reflective tape allows the driver of a commercial vehicle to be seen and to communicate presence with other traffic.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 11.6.2 - Reflective Tape

question: On the Class A Checklist, which item is marked with an asterisk indicating automatic failure if not performed correctly?
choice_a: Battery and frame(s)
choice_c: Air or hydraulic brake check
choice_d: Tires and rims
explanation: The Class A Checklist marks the air or hydraulic brake check with an asterisk, noting automatic failure if not performed correctly.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class A Checklist

question: The Class A Checklist applies to which vehicle configuration(s)?
choice_a: Passenger car with a small utility trailer
choice_c: Motorcycle with sidecar
choice_d: Tractor Semi-Trailer, Truck & Trailer, or Bus & Trailer
explanation: The Class A Checklist heading specifies it covers Tractor Semi-Trailer, Truck & Trailer, or Bus & Trailer configurations.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class A Checklist

question: Under the Class A Checklist, which section lists 'kingpin & apron & gap or drawbar ring & tongue or coupler & tongue'?
choice_a: Combination Vehicles Only
choice_c: Trailer Only
choice_d: Rear of Trailer
explanation: These coupling-related items are grouped under the 'Combination Vehicles Only' section of the Class A Checklist.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class A Checklist

question: Under the Class A Checklist, which items appear specifically under the 'Trailer Only' section?
choice_a: Battery and fuel tank/DEF tank
choice_c: Tires and rims
choice_d: Landing gear & clearance, and reflective tape
explanation: The 'Trailer Only' section of the Class A Checklist lists landing gear & clearance and reflective tape.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class A Checklist

question: According to the rules accompanying the checklists, what must a driver do for each safety critical item to receive credit?
choice_a: Simply check the box next to the item
choice_b: Only verbally state the item's name without gesturing
choice_c: Name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain what is being inspected
choice_d: Physically remove the part for the examiner to see
explanation: The manual states the driver must name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain what is being inspected for each safety critical item, or credit will not be given.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class A Checklist

question: Compared to the Class A Checklist, which sections are absent from the Class B or C Checklist for a Straight Truck or Other Straight Vehicle?
choice_a: Steering Axle
choice_c: Lights Operations Check
choice_d: Combination Vehicles Only and Trailer Only sections
explanation: Because a straight truck has no separate trailer, the Class B or C Straight Truck Checklist omits the Combination Vehicles Only and Trailer Only sections found on the Class A Checklist.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class B or Class C Checklist - Straight Truck or Other Straight Vehicle

question: The Class B or C Checklist for Passenger or School Bus includes which additional sections not found on the Straight Truck/Straight Vehicle version?
choice_a: Trailer Only
choice_b: Passenger and School Bus Only, and School Bus Only
choice_c: Rear of Trailer
choice_d: Combination Vehicles Only
explanation: The Passenger or School Bus version of the Class B or C Checklist adds the Passenger and School Bus Only and School Bus Only sections.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class B or Class C Checklist - Passenger or School Bus

question: On the Class B or C Straight Truck Checklist, what item is listed under 'Rear of Vehicle'?
choice_a: Kingpin & apron
choice_c: Lenses & reflectors
choice_d: Reflective tape
explanation: The Class B or C Straight Truck Checklist lists 'lenses & reflectors' under the Rear of Vehicle section.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class B or Class C Checklist - Straight Truck or Other Straight Vehicle

question: On the Class B or C Checklist (either version), which item is marked with an asterisk for automatic failure if not performed correctly, just as on the Class A Checklist?
choice_a: Wipers & washers
choice_c: Air or hydraulic brake check
choice_d: Frame
explanation: Both Class B/C Checklist versions mark the air or hydraulic brake check with an asterisk for automatic failure if not performed correctly.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Class B or Class C Checklist
